ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A horizontally positioned cylindrical tank contains a transparent liquid filling half of its volume, with air occupying the space above the liquid, as depicted in the cross-sectional diagram. A laser, moving upward along the inner wall of the tank from point P at the bottom, emits a beam that is always directed towards the center point O. When the beam forms a $45^{\circ}$ angle with the vertical direction, the refracted beam exiting the liquid surface into the air becomes just invisible. It is given that the speed of light in air is c.

1. Determine the refractive index $n$ of the liquid.
2. Determine the propagation speed $v$ of the laser in the liquid.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A horizontally positioned cylindrical tank contains a transparent liquid filling half of its volume, with air occupying the space above the liquid, as depicted in the cross-sectional diagram. A laser, moving upward along the inner wall of the tank from point P at the bottom, emits a beam that is always directed towards the center point O. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the cross section of a cylindrical water tank. The upper half inside the circle is labeled Air, and the lower half is labeled Liquid. In the middle there is a horizontal liquid-surface line passing through point O. Point O is on the liquid surface, and through O downward there is a vertical dashed line pointing to the bottom point P; this vertical line represents the normal direction of the liquid surface. A laser is emitted from the inner wall at the lower left, and the ray travels in the liquid toward O, and the figure marks the angle between this incident ray and the vertical direction as 45°. Reasoning: The ray travels from the liquid toward the air and is incident at the liquid surface O; since the liquid surface is horizontal and the normal is vertical, the angle of incidence is the angle between the ray and the vertical direction in the figure, namely theta_i=45°. The problem says the refracted light is "just invisible," indicating that the critical refraction state is reached, with the angle of refraction being 90°, and this angle of incidence is the critical angle from the liquid to the air. Take the refractive index of air as 1 and the refractive index of the liquid as n, then the critical angle satisfies sin theta_c = 1/n. Substituting theta_c=45°, we get sin45°=1/n, so n=1/sin45°=sqrt(2). The propagation speed of light in the liquid satisfies v=c/n, therefore v=c/sqrt(2)=(sqrt(2)/2)c.
